titles.es: Declaraciones de la presidenta

paragraphs.text: Dear colleagues, we have a busy week ahead, and I have a few announcements before we begin.

First of all, this summer Europe experienced yet another record-breaking series of heatwaves. Across our continent, millions of people struggled to cope. Hospital workers fought to protect patients, enduring unsafe temperatures at work. Parents tried to shelter children in buildings unsuited to such extremes. Tragically, many, many thousands of people across our continent lost their lives. Beyond this terrible human cost, the combined threat of extreme heat and wildfires endangered our communities, damaged our ecosystems and cost our economies billions.

Today, as this House mourns those who lost their lives this summer, we turn to the future with determination. And on behalf of this Parliament, I want to thank the brave firefighters and all emergency workers.
(The House rose and gave a standing ovation)
They crossed borders and risked their lives to help others this summer. Now it is up to us in this House to work together so that when the next natural disaster hits, we are better prepared.

Dear colleagues, over the past months and weeks, the crackdown by the regime in Iran continues unabated. The situation remains horrific for so many, particularly young people, whose only crime was to demand the liberty that we take for granted. More and more protesters are being sentenced to death in a desperate attempt by the regime to instil a culture of fear among the people of Iran.

Nothing better illustrates the horror more than the case of twin sisters Tareneh and Romina Rahimi, who were just teenagers when they were dragged from their beds by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps cause last January. Since then, they have endured cruelty beyond what many are capable of bearing.

It took four months for their mother, Marzieh, to learn what had happened to them. By the time she could visit, her daughters were unrecognisable under bruises, limping, with hair ripped out of its roots. There have been reports of torture, threats of rape and sexual violence unless one of them confessed to imagined crimes. Taraneh has been sentenced to death and Romina to a 25-year prison term. Their family has not seen them since the sentence.

Theirs is not an isolated case. There are many, many more stories of the horror inflicted by a regime trying to beat its people into a futile last-gasp attempt at submission and silence. I know that this is an issue close to the hearts of many Members here, and in your name today we tell the 92 million people of Iran that they are not alone, that light will crack through the darkness, and that a regime that uses violence, murder and repression as tools of self-preservation is a regime that is desperate and that understands that it has no legitimacy.

So we will continue to demand the immediate release of Taraneh, Romina and all those unjustly imprisoned. We will not be silent. That is why we took the steps that we did of banning representatives of the regime from our Parliament. That is why we insisted that the IRGC be designated the terrorist organisation we know it to be. And that is why we will keep playing our part to amplify the voice of those demanding freedom.
Cari colleghi, questa Assemblea ha appreso con profondo cordoglio della scomparsa di Emma Bonino.
(Applauso)

Eurodeputata, Commissaria europea, deputata, ministra e senatrice della Repubblica italiana, ha dedicato la sua vita alla difesa della libertà e dell'uguaglianza, contribuendo a costruire una società più giusta.
La sua voce ha lasciato un segno profondo nella politica italiana ed europea. Emma Bonino ha fatto la storia e la sua eredità continuerà a vivere nel lavoro di questo Parlamento.

Dear colleagues, last month this House mourned the passing of another great European, the former Member and President of this House, Klaus Hänsch. We remember him as a principled and courageous European, who steered this Parliament through a time of profound change for our Union.

He worked tirelessly to bring this House closer to Europeans, and was a lifelong champion of a more ambitious, united Europe, with democracy at its centre. His legacy lives on every day in this House, and we will remember him.
I ask you now to please join me in a moment of silence.

titles.es: Comunicación de la presidenta

paragraphs.text: Dear colleagues, it has now been four months since the Council unanimously adopted our proposal to amend the EU Electoral Act to make sure that no Member of this House loses her right to vote just because she is pregnant or a new mother.

The ball is now in the court of the Member States and their national parliaments to ratify the changes. So far, I am happy to announce that Denmark, Bulgaria, Luxembourg and Greece have all completed this process. Ireland, Latvia, Portugal, Romania and Sweden have also confirmed that they are taking the final steps towards ratification.

We thank them for their action and we call on all other Member States and national parliaments to ratify this revision as swiftly as possible. And can I please ask you, dear colleagues, to keep up the pressure at home so that elected representatives are no longer forced to choose between having a family and fulfilling their mandate.

paragraphs.text: Since the adjournment of Parliament's session on 9 July 2026, I have signed, together with the President of the Council, three acts adopted under the ordinary legislative procedure in accordance with Rule 81:
- Empowering Austria to amend its bilateral road transport agreement with Switzerland;
- Exceptional temporary support under the EAFRD;
- The use of technologies by providers of number-independent interpersonal communications services.
I would also like to inform you that on Wednesday I shall sign, together with the President of the Council, two acts adopted under the ordinary legislative procedure:
- Common rules on compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding and of cancellation or long delay of flights;
- The Union Customs Code and the European Union Customs Authority.

titles.es: Comunicaciones de la presidenta

paragraphs.text: This is a big week for us and for Europe. On Wednesday at 09:00, President von der Leyen will debate with us in the State of the European Union session. Then on Thursday at 11:30, Prime Minister of Canada Mark Carney will speak to us in a formal address in this Chamber. These are important moments for our Union, and I truly count on your presence.

Now, last few points. Last week, the Conference of Presidents decided to maintain the following key measures to ensure our plenary sessions are made more accessible, effective and allow for better organisation of Members' work.

We will have fixed start and end timings for debates. This will require everyone to continue to respect the allocated speaking time. This applies to us and to other institutions. Plenary sittings will have a fixed ending time of 20:00 to allow for further meetings and parliamentary work. Any items added at the opening of the part-session will be scheduled during an extended slot, held from 20:00 to 21:00.
The Council and Commission will continue to be able to intervene spontaneously during debates.
On Tuesday at 15:00, a debate with the Commission will be scheduled, with the presentation of a proposal adopted in the College meeting on the same day or a Question Time with the Commission.
Blue cards and catch-the-eye will be allowed with more flexibility.

These changes will mean that the special format for key debates with randomised speakers' lists will no longer be needed and, therefore, be discontinued. The rules on personal statements will continue to be enforced.
Let me take this opportunity to remind you that tomorrow and on Wednesday, the debates will start immediately after the vote.
Once again, I thank you for your cooperation and for your efforts. It is your contribution that made this initiative a success.

titles.es: Orden de los trabajos

paragraphs.text: We now come to the order of business. The final draft agenda, as adopted by the Conference of Presidents on 9 September 2026 pursuant to Rule 163, has been distributed.

I would like to inform you that I have received a request for an urgent procedure from the ENVI Committee, pursuant to Rule 170(5), on 'Revised heat and fuel benchmark values for 2026-2030'. The vote on this request will be taken tomorrow and, if adopted, the vote will be held at a future part-session.
With the agreement of the political groups, I wish to put to the House the following proposal for a change to the final draft agenda. On Wednesday, the following item will be added to the votes:
- Objection pursuant to Rule 115(2), (3) and (4)(c): maximum residue levels for flupyradifurone.
The deadlines are: amendments, today at 19:00; splits and separates, tomorrow at 16:00.
We now move to changes requested by political groups.

For today, the Greens/EFA Group has requested that a Commission statement on 'Brutal government crackdown on the LGBTIQ+ community in Türkiye’ be added as the last item before the one-minute speeches. As a consequence, the sitting would be extended to 21:00.

I have also received an alternative title from the S&D Group. I understand that a compromise was reached, but I need you to confirm between the two groups on the following title: 'Government crackdown on the LGBTIQ+ community in Türkiye: Türkiye's compliance with its international commitments on non-discrimination'.
I give the floor to Terry Reintke to move the request.

That is completely unacceptable and this Parliament has to take a clear stance against this new authoritarian wave in Türkiye.

If we do not speak up now, colleagues, this will continue and the LGBTI community in Türkiye will be further targeted. We owe it to them, to my chosen family and to our friends in Türkiye that we speak up and that is why we are proposing a debate with the proposed title, but we are also very happy with the compromise that has been found, so please let us add this item to the agenda tonight.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, a decisão do Banco Central Europeu de aumentar as taxas de juro é uma decisão com consequências graves, e o Parlamento Europeu não deve passar‑lhe ao lado. Esta decisão não ataca as causas reais do atual quadro inflacionário, mas penaliza duplamente os trabalhadores e as populações com o aumento do custo de vida, atinge as pequenas e médias empresas, que veem dificultado o acesso ao financiamento e, simultaneamente, favorece a banca e o setor financeiro, que continuarão a avolumar os lucros que vão recolhendo.

Para combater o atual quadro inflacionário, é preciso travar a agressão dos Estados Unidos ao Irão e a desestabilização do Médio Oriente, que faz aumentar os preços dos combustíveis, que perturba os circuitos internacionais de abastecimentos. É preciso travar o aumento do custo de vida que os povos estão a sofrer com o aumento da energia dos combustíveis e dos bens essenciais, a que agora se acrescenta o aumento dos custos com a habitação. É preciso regular preços e impedir o aumento dos custos com a habitação e, naturalmente, distribuir também os lucros que a banca está a avolumar para que o custo e o fardo sobre os povos não cresçam.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidente, esta semana debatimos en este Parlamento la libertad de prensa de Hong Kong, pero el Ministerio del Interior de un Estado miembro, como es España, ha elaborado un documento con 280 periodistas clasificados por su ideología y por su posición ante el Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez: a unos, para señalarlos; a otros, para premiarlos con programas, sueldos e información privilegiada.

Yo mismo he denunciado ante la justicia española y la Comisión Europea, el pasado 9 de septiembre, no solo esta lista ilegal del Gobierno español, sino también seguimientos ilegales del Gobierno a algunos miembros de la oposición de nuestro país. Esta Cámara aprobó el Reglamento Europeo sobre la Libertad de los Medios de Comunicación para impedir exactamente esto.
¿Qué hacemos? ¿Miramos a Hong Kong, pero ignoramos lo que ocurre en Europa? Por eso pido que se incluya de urgencia en el orden del día, presidente.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, pochissimi giorni fa, vicino a Firenze, alla mia città, una donna di 45 anni, Lorena, è stata brutalmente uccisa dal suo ex compagno, che l'ha scaraventata dal viadotto di un'autostrada.

È il femminicidio numero 34 in Italia, dove l'86% degli omicidi di donne avviene per mano di un partner o di un familiare. E in Europa, 19 Stati su 27 comunicano in modo coerente i dati sui femminicidi. Gli altri non lo fanno.

Per questo, questo Parlamento, colleghi, deve vigilare sulla Commissione e gli Stati membri affinché la direttiva del 2024 sia pienamente attuata entro giugno dell'anno prossimo, anche alla luce della storica risoluzione che abbiamo approvato a larghissima maggioranza, nonostante in quest'Aula vi siano membri, come quelli del gruppo delle nazioni sovrane, come ad esempio, Roberto Vannacci, che sostengono che il femminicidio non esista e che ci vogliono far tornare a mezzo secolo fa, al tempo del delitto d'onore.
Per questo dobbiamo impegnarci sempre di più per rispetto di quelle migliaia di donne che ogni giorno vivono nell'angoscia e chiedono protezione e riconoscimento dalle istituzioni.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Ich beziehe mich auf Artikel 10 Absatz 1 der Geschäftsordnung in Verbindung mit dem Demokratieprinzip des Artikels 2 EUV. Der grüne Abgeordnete Daniel Freund hat bereits vor der Regierungsbildung in Sachsen-Anhalt das potenzielle Einfrieren von EU-Mitteln im Falle einer AfD-Regierung gefordert. Er begründet dies unter anderem damit, dass eine Schlechterstellung in Form von Sanktionen zu einem genehmen Regierungswechsel führen könnte.

Seine Forderung stellt damit einen erheblichen Eingriff gegen demokratische Prozesse dar. Besonders kritisch ist der Vorschlag, wenn man bedenkt, dass aus den EU-Mitteln unter anderem Schulrenovierungen und Kindertagesstätten unterstützt werden, was Herrn Freund als Haushaltspolitiker sehr wohl bekannt sein sollte. Es scheint offenbar der Wunsch zu sein, Schüler und Kinder schlechter zu stellen, weil einem die potenzielle Regierung nicht passt.

Auf dem Rücken der Schwächsten wird versucht, durch juristische Spielchen Einfluss auf Wahlen zu nehmen – das ist schäbig. Und diese Erpressung durch die Grünen werden sich die Bürger in Sachsen-Anhalt nicht bieten lassen.

paragraphs.text: Ich wusste nicht, dass wir hier Anträge zur Geschäftsordnung machen können, wenn uns die Meinung eines Kollegen nicht passt. Aber wo wir jetzt schon hier sind: Ich habe einfach nur daran erinnert, dass es ein sehr klares EU-Recht gibt.

Ich kann Ihnen nur empfehlen: Schauen Sie mal in die Haushaltsordnung der Europäischen Union. Wenn man sich nicht an die Grundwerte und an die Gesetze der Union hält, dann verwirkt man auch das Recht auf EU-Gelder. Das ist eine völlig klare Gesetzeslage, hat nichts mit Wahlen oder so zu tun.

Aber wenn man eben ein Wahlprogramm schreibt, das verspricht, die EU-Werte zu brechen – und auch nicht nur ein- oder zweimal, sondern systematisch –, naja, dann steht einem im Zweifel dieselbe Konsequenz aus, die die Kollegen Viktor Orbán oder auch die Regierung von Herrn Kaczyński in Polen auch schon erfahren haben. Und sollte die AfD in Sachsen Anhalt an die Macht kommen, dann dient auch das.

Was den Kinderschutz angeht, kann ich nur empfehlen – Sie haben einen Parteikollegen, der Kinder mit Baseballschlägern angreift: Vielleicht sollten Sie sich darum kümmern, anstatt hier solche Geschäftsordnungsanträge zu stellen.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Ich beziehe mich auf Artikel 167 der Geschäftsordnung. Die Ukraine versinkt immer mehr im Chaos. Ein Generalstaatsanwalt, der selbst der Korruption beschuldigt wurde, hat sich außer Landes abgesetzt. Es gab Schusswechsel zwischen Sicherheitsbehörden. Und jetzt hat man die ehemalige Pressesprecherin von Herrn Selenskyj sanktioniert, durch Herrn Selenskyj, weil sie sich gegen eine NATO Perspektive der Ukraine ausgesprochen hat, weil sie sich für den Frieden engagiert und weil sie sich gegen die Zwangsrekrutierung junger Männer ausgesprochen hat. Dabei hat sie immer die Angriffe Russlands auch verurteilt. Und ich finde, wenn solche Zustände in der Ukraine herrschen, wenn sie sich immer mehr zu einem Mafiastaat entwickelt, dann muss dieses Europäische Parlament nicht einfach immer nur mit dem Kopf weitere Milliarden abnicken, sondern dieses endlich in das Zentrum der Debatte stellen.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, this point of order is according to Rule 40.

Since 2021, 37 000 tonnes of PFAS-containing hazardous waste was illegally imported from Slovenia, Italy and Germany and disposed of in Croatia, in the city of Gospić – the birthplace of Nikola Tesla, the genius inventor of modern electricity.

Gospić and the County of Lika are one of the most beautiful natural preserved parts of Croatia, proud of their clean water and healthy food. Yet the weak Government, weak state inspections, the regulation of national rules and corruption enable this pan-European criminal eco-cide in the Schengen Area.
I call on us all to show solidarity with the citizens of Gospić. I call immediately to stop toxic waste exports to Croatia and to help with urgent waste clean-up processes.
We shall not allow Croatia or any Member State to become an EU toxic waste landfill.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, three weeks ago, my colleague Hanna Gedin and I were due to travel on a parliamentary mission to the Israeli‑occupied West Bank and to East Jerusalem. We were scheduled to meet with Save the Children and the EU mission, visit refugee camps, and meet with Palestinian as well as Israeli human rights organisations. Although we had obtained authorisation to enter Israel, we were denied entry. The Foreign Minister, Gideon Sa'ar, justified the decision on the grounds that we have criticised Israel's extensive abuses and genocide against Palestinians.

I would first like to thank you and your cabinet for the swift and firm support you provided when Israel took this unacceptable decision. However, I would also like you as President to consider what further measures this Parliament should take in response to Israel systematically preventing parliamentarians from entering the occupied Palestinian territories.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, under Rule 40, like every Strasbourg session, you keep coming up with new ways to make our debates more engaging. But here's a better idea: get rid of the ridiculous rule that lets Members refuse a blue‑card question. It is unbelievable. The left side of this Chamber acts like an applause machine. They clap on cue. They cheer each other on like a squad of North Korean cheerleaders. But the moment someone asks them to defend what they have just said, then they hide behind a procedural rule and refuse to answer questions. In any parliament worthy of the name, you do not get to dodge accountability. So, as long as that absurd rule remains, please stop trying to reinvent our debate because you have to fix what is broken first.

So, as long as that absurd rule remains, please stop trying to reinvent our debate because you have to fix what is broken first.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, let me be frank: a vote tomorrow against CBAM is a vote against European industry and European workers.

I could almost not believe my eyes when I saw that some so-called nationalist groups on the right have tabled an amendment to reject CBAM altogether. Because rejecting CBAM means rejecting a level playing field, it means putting the limited interests of large global multinationals above those of the many European industries and workers. And yet the same people that are sceptical of CBAM come to me and ask whether certain CN codes can be added to the list, which is a bit strange. Either you are against it, or you support it and try to create a situation where our industry is protected.

Dear colleagues, you cannot have your cake and eat it too. And to me that confirms the quiet part out loud: CBAM works. Look at the world: China, Canada, Türkiye, Japan, South Korea, Morocco – and the list keeps growing – are putting carbon prices or emission trading systems in place. This shows something very important: that when Europe leads, others follow. And that is exactly what European citizens and businesses are asking from us, especially now. It's something that is making me proud, something that we all should be proud of.

CBAM is effective, and with the agreement we vote on tomorrow, it will be even more effective. We've strengthened CBAM against circumvention. We've addressed carbon leakage more thoroughly, and we further strengthened the level playing field for European industry. Crucially, for our industry, we found a solution on Article 27a. This Article prevents investments in technologies of the future and punishes those that have already moved ahead. Certainty is essential for investors and businesses, and that's something we should give them.

Allowing the Commission, through a delegated act and without Parliament, to pause CBAM for certain goods at any given time would undermine precisely that certainty. And that is why, from the beginning and across the different opinion-giving committees, the political groups were clear: Article 7 has to go while addressing the concerns of, for example, the farmers. Instead of creating a disguised subsidy for foreign fertilisers, we keep the mechanism intact and redirect CBAM revenues to affected sectors in case of serious and unforeseen circumstances. We also found another solution through the Temporary Decarbonisation Fund, on which our colleague Pascal Canfin has done excellent work. We extended its scope to agricultural products: exactly what the groups behind this compromise wanted from the start.

So tomorrow we do take note of who's there and who's missing. Let's see who is willing to stand up and deliver for industry, workers and farmers. And I expect everyone who is concerned about farmers to call their Member States and their permanent representations to urge them to unblock the work on the Temporary Decarbonisation Fund in the Council and to continue the work there as quickly as possible.

Finally, I would like to thank all the political groups for their constructive approach during these negotiations: we've reached a fair and balanced agreement, one that protects industry and workers, reinforces our climate ambition and ensures that the polluters pay. I look forward to the upcoming trilogue so that we can conclude the work on the CBAM extension as soon as possible and provide much-needed certainty for Europe, industry, our investors, and especially our workers.

paragraphs.text: Madame la présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, aujourd'hui, c'est un jour important puisque cela fait des années que le Parlement européen demande à ce qu'il y ait, pour protéger nos industriels qui exportent vers des marchés, vers des pays où il n'y a pas de prix du carbone – cela fait des années que le Parlement européen demande un outil spécifique pour accompagner nos exportateurs de façon à compenser le désavantage concurrentiel qu'ils subissent en ayant, eux, un prix du carbone qu'ils payent en Europe sur des marchés à l'export qui n'ont pas de prix du carbone.

Cela faisait des années qu'on nous disait que ce n'était pas possible, et puis finalement, la Commission européenne a proposé un fonds de décarbonation temporaire qui répond exactement à cet enjeu. Je suis ravi de voir qu'il y a dans cette enceinte un très large soutien à ce type d'outil, contrairement au Conseil, puisque les États membres, eux, n'avancent pas dans cette négociation.

J'espère que cette semaine, en ayant voté et en ayant voté le plus largement possible en faveur de ce fonds, on enverra un signal très fort. D'ailleurs, je note, Monsieur le Commissaire, que vous n'avez vous-même pas repris un tel mécanisme dans votre nouvelle proposition de marché du carbone. Je suis très surpris, parce que le besoin de protéger nos exportateurs contre la concurrence déloyale liée à l'absence de prix du carbone sur les marchés export va demeurer dans la durée au delà de ce fonds de décarbonation temporaire qui commence dès que possible, dès que nous l'aurons voté, jusqu'en 2030.

Il répond donc, ce fonds, à un enjeu très clair, une attente des industriels, et c'est très bien de donner corps à cette attente. Mais à côté, il y a aussi la question des agriculteurs – mon collègue Mohammed Chahim vient d'y faire référence. Nous avons parfaitement conscience que lorsque l'on met en place un prix du carbone sur les engrais qui sont utilisés par les agriculteurs, eh bien cela rehausse le prix des engrais. Même si, il faut toujours le rappeler, c'est une toute petite partie dans l'augmentation qui a été effective l'année dernière du prix des engrais, qui est liée essentiellement au prix du gaz et à la crise dans le détroit d'Ormuz, et par ailleurs au comportement de la Russie qui maîtrise ce marché du gaz mondial.

Donc ne nous trompons pas de combat: la priorité si l'on veut réduire la dépendance aux engrais et à leur évolution sur le prix mondial, c'est de décarboner notre agriculture et c'est aussi de produire en Européens.

Et c'est pour cela que nous avons, ensemble, avec Mohammed Chahim, conçu cette réforme du Fonds temporaire de décarbonation pour permettre aux agriculteurs qui exportent du blé, par exemple, des céréales, qui sont donc eux-mêmes en concurrence sur des marchés export, par exemple au Moyen-Orient, avec des producteurs russes qui, eux, ne payent pas le prix du carbone, d'avoir une compensation financière – non pas en supprimant le mécanisme d'ajustement carbone pour les engrais, non pas en créant une incertitude radicale, qui a été dénoncée par les industriels, qui était la proposition initiale de la Commission, à savoir donner à la Commission la possibilité de suspendre un secteur à tout moment du champ du MCAF, ruinant ainsi la prévisibilité que le MCAF apporte – mais sans nier qu'il y a effectivement un problème à résoudre spécifiquement pour nos agriculteurs et le prix des engrais.

C'est pour ça que la solution que nous avons trouvée tous ensemble, la droite et la gauche, de façon pragmatique, j'espère que nous pourrons la soutenir largement en plénière. Je crois que ce sera le cas, je m'en réjouis car nous pourrons ainsi la négocier fortement dans le cadre des trilogues qui vont commencer avec les autres institutions.

Merci pour votre soutien large. Je pense que sur ce sujet, il ne faut pas faire de politique politicienne, il faut être pragmatique, ambitieux et garder en permanence le cap de la décarbonation comme étant un élément de souveraineté. Et je regrette qu'encore une fois, les députés d'extrême droite, plutôt que de mener cette bataille préfèrent détruire le MCAF au nom d'une idéologie anti-climat qui est totalement primaire et désuète après l'été que nous venons malheureusement de passer.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, colleagues, 20 years ago, Europe did something no one had done before – it set up the world's first and largest international carbon market. Since then, the EU Emissions Trading System has reduced emissions and driven industrial decarbonisation. Yet, like any system that exists for a long time, it needs to be adapted to a changing world, while still reaching its objectives, and this is why where we are today.

We are at the beginning of one of the most important debates that will define Europe's climate and industrial policy for the years to come. We face a challenge: aligning our ambition with the EU's climate targets, while strengthening the competitiveness of our industry. It's not easy, but we must get it right. At the heart of this debate is the market stability reserve. It plays a key function in the ETS – almost like a 'central bank' of emissions quotas – by preventing price volatility and maintaining market stability. In short, it gives predictability to the ETS, and this is fundamental because a carbon market that is unpredictable drives industry away without reducing a single tonne of CO2.

In April, the Commission proposed to cancel the invalidation mechanism of the reserve, allowing it to grow above the 400‑million ceiling. The rationale is clear: to give the carbon market and industries a bit more breathing space. But abolishing the invalidation mechanism entirely, without knowing what the ETS will look like after the reform, raises legitimate questions.

While this proposal does not rewrite the ETS, it marks the opening chapter of the comprehensive review of the system. How we handle it will set the tone for the debates that follow. That's why I am proud and honoured to present, as rapporteur and ENVI Chair, the compromise that we found on the MSR proposal.

It consists of two main elements. First, we keep the invalidation mechanism. It stays to avoid excessive oversupply and ensure credibility of the ETS. But, importantly, we raise the invalidation ceiling from 400 to 650 million allowances. This gives the reserve more capacity and flexibility to respond to stocks.

Second, we delay entry into force of this new ceiling. Having a clear starting date – and we propose 1 March 2027 – will give clarity and smoothen the transition. These are the elements of the deal that we have shaped with political groups and shadow rapporteurs, whom I thank for their work. It's a deal that presents a pragmatic and balanced solution and has received strong support in the ENVI Committee.

But, importantly, the compromise that I present to you today strikes the right balance that we should aim for in the broader ETS review, keeping the ETS credible as a climate instrument and making it work for European industry. Decarbonisation and competitiveness should not be seen as opposing goals – they are not.

Colleagues, the ETS revision is one of the defining industrial and climate policy debates of this legislature. Today's vote on the MSR is the first step. I therefore ask you to vote in favour of our text in plenary tomorrow and give us a clear mandate to start a negotiation with the Member States. Let us set the right tone for the discussion ahead.

interventions.speaker_label: Wopke Hoekstra, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, apologies. It's as I said to you before, drinking too much milk, that's what you get.

Madam President, honourable Members, very good to see you and many thanks to the three rapporteurs for elaborating on the three different instruments that we have in front of us. Different, but all, I would argue, with a very common purpose: keeping Europe on track in terms of its decarbonisation and at the same time safeguarding our industry's competitiveness and making sure we do not see any carbon leakage. Please allow me to briefly speak on all three of them.

First on CBAM, truly a key instrument for advancing Europe's clean industrial transition. By addressing the risk of carbon leakage, it strengthens clearly the EU's competitiveness, it supports investments in decarbonisation and, of course, it reinforces our strategic independence. It brings all those three elements hand in hand. Now, last December, with the help of this Parliament, the Commission has already proposed to radically simplify the design and we have succeeded together on that one. We have also proposed to strengthen CBAM and that is the proposal Mr Chahim just spoke about. We proposed extending CBAM to certain steel- and aluminium‑intensive downstream products, reinforcing our anti‑circumvention measures and, importantly, adjusting electricity rules. We put forward this proposal after truly extensive discussions, collaborations, interactions with industry, which have made – I am sure also to the esteemed Members of this House – crystal clear that CBAM contained too many loopholes to be fully effective.

Madam Chair, let me please turn now to the temporary decarbonisation fund. Here as well, in December 2025, we proposed this fund and we did so to provide temporary support for decarbonisation in 2026 and in 2027. It is aimed specifically at operators of EU ETS installations producing CBAM goods that are still considered to face a higher risk of carbon leakage. So, EU producers will need to show they are taking steps to decarbonise to receive support where the funding can then help to invest in the long‑term decarbonisation of their production. In my view, this proposal strikes a delicate balance between ensuring that the fund is effective while at the same time limiting administrative burden for operators, as it should. This is achieved by aligning the fund's management with existing EU ETS infrastructure and processes.

Now, on both the files, while we still reserve as a Commission our position on the different amendments at this stage, we very much welcome Parliament's overall support and the speed at which it has adopted its report. Allow me to once again emphasise that for this revision, speed continues to be of the essence. We do many things well in Europe, but we typically do them too slowly. So, it is key to start the trilogue negotiations as early as possible with a view of reaching a political agreement well before the end of this calendar year. Without such an agreement, let me be clear on that as well, there is a risk. There is a risk that the downstream extension simply cannot enter into force on 1 January 2028 as planned.

Madam Chair, third, the market stability reserve. Could I say, that has been a real success. It has helped clear the historical surplus of allowances and it has, frankly speaking, been essential to keeping the EU carbon market functioning well. At the same time, market conditions are becoming tighter. So, the MSR therefore needs to evolve as well. To that end, the Commission has come forward with a targeted amendment to the MSR decision that would end the invalidation of allowances. A sufficiently large MSR is needed, in our view, as a buffer for both liquidity and also stability. It allows the EU ETS to manage changing market conditions by withdrawing allowances where there is a significant surplus while still keeping enough capacity to respond if scarcity emerges. And of course, it also helps addressing excessive price fluctuations in case we would see them. Under the current rules, however, allowances above the 400 million threshold continue to be permanently invalidated. At the same time, future intakes into the reserve are expected to decline substantially. This further highlights the importance of preserving the allowances already in the reserve, rather than continuing to invalidate them.

So, honourable Members, to wrap up, across these three files, I would argue that our objective is the same: a carbon market that delivers decarbonisation, that strengthens European competitiveness and gives investment certainty, and that is always the request of all of our companies. I would very much like to thank all the three rapporteurs for their great work. Their reports, in my view, demonstrate our shared determination to make CBAM and the temporary decarbonisation fund effective instruments, as well as to ensure that the MSR has enough firepower now and in the near future.

Madam Chair, let me please turn now to the temporary decarbonisation fund. Here as well, in December 2025, we proposed this fund and we did so to provide temporary support for decarbonisation in 2026 and in 2027. It is aimed specifically at operators of EU ETS installations producing CBAM goods that are still considered to face a higher risk of carbon leakage. So, EU producers will need to show they are taking steps to decarbonise to receive support where the funding can then help to invest in the long‑term decarbonisation of their production. In my view, this proposal strikes a delicate balance between ensuring that the fund is effective while at the same time limiting administrative burden for operators, as it should. This is achieved by aligning the fund's management with existing EU ETS infrastructure and processes.

Now, on both the files, while we still reserve as a Commission our position on the different amendments at this stage, we very much welcome Parliament's overall support and the speed at which it has adopted its report. Allow me to once again emphasise that for this revision, speed continues to be of the essence. We do many things well in Europe, but we typically do them too slowly. So, it is key to start the trilogue negotiations as early as possible with a view of reaching a political agreement well before the end of this calendar year. Without such an agreement, let me be clear on that as well, there is a risk. There is a risk that the downstream extension simply cannot enter into force on 1 January 2028 as planned.

Madam Chair, third, the market stability reserve. Could I say, that has been a real success. It has helped clear the historical surplus of allowances and it has, frankly speaking, been essential to keeping the EU carbon market functioning well. At the same time, market conditions are becoming tighter. So, the MSR therefore needs to evolve as well. To that end, the Commission has come forward with a targeted amendment to the MSR decision that would end the invalidation of allowances. A sufficiently large MSR is needed, in our view, as a buffer for both liquidity and also stability. It allows the EU ETS to manage changing market conditions by withdrawing allowances where there is a significant surplus while still keeping enough capacity to respond if scarcity emerges. And of course, it also helps addressing excessive price fluctuations in case we would see them. Under the current rules, however, allowances above the 400 million threshold continue to be permanently invalidated. At the same time, future intakes into the reserve are expected to decline substantially. This further highlights the importance of preserving the allowances already in the reserve, rather than continuing to invalidate them.

So, honourable Members, to wrap up, across these three files, I would argue that our objective is the same: a carbon market that delivers decarbonisation, that strengthens European competitiveness and gives investment certainty, and that is always the request of all of our companies. I would very much like to thank all the three rapporteurs for their great work. Their reports, in my view, demonstrate our shared determination to make CBAM and the temporary decarbonisation fund effective instruments, as well as to ensure that the MSR has enough firepower now and in the near future.

interventions.speaker_label: Lynn Boylan, rapporteur for the opinion of the INTA Committee.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: rapporteur for the opinion of the INTA Committee

paragraphs.text: President, colleagues, Commissioner, as the Left shadow for CBAM and TDF and as the rapporteur for the INTA opinion, I would like to take the opportunity to thank both the rapporteurs for their commitment.
I think we have a strong agreement on key points, where we expand the CBAM without undermining it, and we also bring more global justice to the CBAM.

We believe in this policy, but we need others around the world to believe in it too, so we have included clear signals to trade partners that CBAM is not punitive or protectionist, but a true climate measure. This means commitments on technical assistance, removing barriers to SMEs in least-developed countries, and leading global cooperation on decarbonisation.

Most importantly, we maintain Parliament’s call that monies under CBAM and TDF can be used as a source of additional climate finance. The climate crisis demands that we start to deliver on climate finance and technology-sharing going to developing countries.
This is why CBAM must be accompanied by new climate finance to make it a real global climate action measure.

interventions.speaker_label: Sandra Gómez López, ponente de opinión de la Comisión BUDG.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: ponente de opinión de la Comisión BUDG

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, permítanme que ponga el acento en que el debate de hoy va más allá de política climática. También va de cómo financiamos el futuro de la Unión Europea, ya que precisamente el Mecanismo de Ajuste en Frontera por Carbono es uno de los candidatos a formar parte de la cesta de recursos propios desde el año 2020, para que, entre otras cosas, contribuya precisamente a la financiación de la deuda de los NextGenerationEU. Pese a la necesidad de que este recurso entre en funcionamiento, el Consejo lo tiene bloqueado desde el año 2020. Mientras tanto, han surgido nuevas prioridades: hablamos de transición energética, de competitividad industrial o de defensa, y no podemos seguir aumentando las responsabilidades de la Unión Europea sin aumentar también la capacidad de financiación. Por eso, la ampliación del Mecanismo de Ajuste en Frontera por Carbono puede contribuir a solucionar parte de este problema, ya que se calcula que puede generar alrededor de 580 millones de euros en el año 2030 y 690 millones de euros en el 2035.
Por lo tanto, quiero aprovechar para concluir haciendo un llamamiento al Consejo para que desbloquee un recurso de vital importancia para la Unión Europea.

interventions.speaker_label: Danuše Nerudová, rapporteur for the opinion of the BUDG Committee.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: rapporteur for the opinion of the BUDG Committee

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, the EU has set higher climate goals and strict rules for our companies, while their competitors outside Europe often face much lower standards. With enough investment, especially in the decarbonisation of heavy industry, these goals and rules will remain just words on paper, or worse, become a burden.

This temporary mechanism can help, but we need two things: first, it must not become another bureaucratic monster; and second, all the money has to go back to our companies, not disappear into national budgets and be spent elsewhere. We have seen this with ETS revenues. Let us not make the same mistake again.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, signor Commissario, onorevoli colleghi, noi abbiamo lavorato seriamente. Io credo e ringrazio i relatori delle altre famiglie politiche per dare compimento ad una giustissima decisione della Commissione europea: di procedere non solo a rinforzare il CBAM, ma a ridefinirne lo scopo, allargandolo.
Questo perché? E di questo devo dare atto al collega Adam JARUBAS, relatore, di aver fatto un lavoro di sintesi decisamente non facile.

Lo scopo è quello di creare le condizioni perché non si contraddica la misura al suo interno. Cioè, salvando il primo anello della catena – il caso, ad esempio, dell’acciaio è stato eclatante – e non salvando i successivi anelli, si finisce per esaurire completamente il valore della misura.

Allora, intervenire allargando lo scopo anche ai prodotti trasformati consente a chi è stato tutelato nella fase iniziale della misura di ottenere piena soddisfazione e, quindi, dare ristoro vero all'industria europea.
Credo sarà un ottimo lavoro, con un ottimo effetto anche sulla revisione dell’ETS.

Ως εισηγητής για το Ευρωπαϊκό Λαϊκό Κόμμα, είμαι περήφανος, γιατί το Προσωρινό Ταμείο Απανθρακοποίησης δίνει ανάσα σε πολύ σημαντικούς κλάδους, όπως το αλουμίνιο και το τσιμέντο —κλάδοι κρίσιμοι για την Ευρώπη και ιδιαίτερα για την Κύπρο. Το Ταμείο αυτό είναι ένα από τα πολλά εργαλεία που επεξεργαζόμαστε για να αυξήσουμε την ανταγωνιστικότητα της Ευρώπης.

Οι ευρωπαϊκές επιχειρήσεις ανταγωνίζονται διεθνώς χώρες χωρίς μηχανισμούς CBAM και χάνουν συνεχώς μερίδιο αγοράς. Με αυτό το στοχευμένο εργαλείο, στηρίζουμε την ανταγωνιστικότητα και ταυτόχρονα χρηματοδοτούμε πραγματικές επενδύσεις απανθρακοποίησης.
Το Ευρωπαϊκό Κοινοβούλιο έκανε το καθήκον του. Προτείνουμε μια φιλόδοξη λύση για τη βιομηχανία και το περιβάλλον. Τώρα είναι η σειρά των κρατών μελών να σπάσουν το αδιέξοδο στο Συμβούλιο.

interventions.speaker_label: Annalisa Corrado, a nome del gruppo S&D.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, si parla spesso di transizione ecologica e decarbonizzazione, legandole al rischio di deindustrializzazione che attraversa purtroppo l'Unione europea. Un rischio che non riguarda però allo stesso modo tutti i settori: è totalmente falso, ad esempio, che sia un problema per il settore energetico, dove decarbonizzazione e competitività coincidono totalmente, mentre esiste per i settori manifatturieri esposti a concorrenza sleale.

La risposta non è distruggere le nostre ambizioni nella tutela dell'ecosistema e nell'affrontare la crisi climatica ma mettere in campo la forza dell'Unione. Il CBAM è un esempio concreto, è un principio semplice: alle imprese europee chiediamo giustamente di ridurre le proprie emissioni, innovare, investire nella decarbonizzazione.

Ma questo sforzo ha un costo e non possiamo permettere che diventi uno svantaggio competitivo rispetto a chi produce fuori dall'Europa senza curarsi dei costi ambientali e sociali. Il CBAM nasce per questo: ristabilire condizioni di concorrenza più eque e tutelare la nostra industria di qualità.

Oggi facciamo un passo avanti estendendo questa protezione lungo la catena del valore. Non solo l'acciaio e l'alluminio ma anche i prodotti che li utilizzano, dagli elettrodomestici alle attrezzature, ai componenti industriali. Rispetto a 180 prodotti inizialmente proposti, arriviamo a oltre 450.

Allo stesso tempo rafforziamo i controlli su chi cerca di fare il furbo, perché un CBAM efficace deve essere solido, prevedibile e capace di dare certezza alle imprese che investono nella transizione.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, colleagues, surprisingly, I am not so optimistic: some improvements in ETS and CBAM go in a good direction, and Patriots will be able to support them. But just be clear: these are only very cosmetic changes targeting symptoms and not the cause of EU industry downfall. In medicinal terminology, EU industry is a critical-state, dying patient poisoned by wrong industrial and climate policy of the past years – a patient that needs a real antidote and not just soft painkillers.

In the reality, EU industry needs a much cheaper ETS, one price for EU exporters, an effective, uninterrupted CBAM to protect EU market and ... (inaudible) compensations for some sectors such as for farmers – simple measures that are not at all reached by the small improvement that we have today on the table.

The more alarming is to hear that you consider these good but soft measures as sufficient, completely ignoring the critical signals from industry across Europe. Trust us, Mr Commissioner, industry needs much more, and every delay to deliver real corrections in the climate policy from your side is a damage for Europe. The choice is very simple: either you protect EU industry from wrong EU climate policy of the past years, or you continue in this policy far from global reality based on unrealistic targets and damaging our European economy. So what will be your choice, Mr Commissioner?

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, good evening. I think that high energy prices are the largest headache for everybody in Europe: for the people, business and industries. That is why we are lagging behind the US, China and other competing powers.
It is very clear what we must do: we need stable prices of the ETS allowances, particularly now, so we need to improve sectoral imbalances and avoid the risk of allowance scarcity and price spikes.

I am always very critical of the Commission, but now I would be applauding it because it understood the assignment and you, Commissioner, have come up with a simple proposal for the reform of MSR 1: to stop the invalidation of allowances and build a big enough reserve. Full stop. I applaud this.

The EPP could have a simple majority in the Committee to support this. But because of this policy of firewalls, it decided to negotiate with the left to give a green flavour to this so-called compromise.

The ECR is different. I will simply propose to my colleagues to reject the Committee's so-called compromise, and to stay behind your proposal in tomorrow's vote. That is the only reasonable way forward.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Renew Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, it feels like I am living in two different realities: one where we have had the most extreme summers in Europe, where Parisians have literally been boiling and cooking eggs on their rooftops, where Europe has had massive wildfires, where 35 000 Europeans have died prematurely, where we have had massive wildfires across the continent, and where scientists say that we have already surpassed 1.5 °C.

And then we have the other reality: the one where competitiveness has become the argument for dismantling climate policy, where competitiveness is used to oppose technological development, where political forces ask to dismantle the 'polluter pays principle' and to protect the fossil industry.

How can we have these two realities at the same time? How did we end up here? Why are we discussing things in this room, pretending that this summer didn't happen? This summer shows that we cannot slow down the reduction of emissions, that we cannot lower the ambitions of the Emissions Trading Scheme and that we cannot dismantle the Market Stability Reserve as the Commission is proposing.

We in this House – the House of Europeans – we speak up. We will resist and we oppose this change. We do not always agree with each other, the political forces of this House. But we have found a joint proposal and we are challenging the European Commission when we are obviously trying to live in two realities at the same time. We need to live in one reality and we need to fix this.

interventions.speaker_label: Sara Matthieu, on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, why should a washing machine made in Europe cost more simply because our European producers pay for their carbon emissions, and a Chinese producer doesn't? That's why we built CBAM, and tomorrow we take the next step by extending it from the raw steel and aluminium to the finished products. And thanks to the Greens, we've extended this to essential green tech products like solar panels, like heat pumps.

We also removed the so-called emergency brake that would have left the door open for products to be removed from the scope. There were some conservatives who wanted to keep that possibility, but that, colleagues, would have created uncertainty for our companies, and by removing it we are making CBAM more predictable and keeping investment security.

So all in all we will have a stronger CBAM. We are making polluting imports pay for their carbon costs, we are making clean investment more attractive, and we give European industry the confidence they need to invest here.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, there is nothing – no data, no science – which says that we have the option of slowing down cutting emissions.

Extreme heatwaves are killing people and destroying crops. Yet here we are, in Parliament, faced with several proposals to change the Emissions Trading System, which would mean slowing down the pace. That is unacceptable.

The ETS is a market-based mechanism, meaning that it only works if there is scarcity. If there is an oversupply of emission allowances, emissions will not decrease. That is why the invalidation mechanism in the MSR is so important: it manages expectations. We cannot afford the risk that releasing additional allowances from the MSR in the future will drive up emissions.
I am very happy that there are groups that are willing to improve on these proposals that we get from the Commission, for example on the Market Stability Reserve.
But it's also a problem for us when we end up making them a little bit better, but still end up in a situation that is worse than when we started out, lowering ambitions. We really have to do better.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Stahlwerke in der EU unterliegen horrenden CO2-Abgaben durch das Emissionshandelssystem. Deswegen wurde europäischer Stahl teurer und wurde lieber importiert. Die Einnahmen der Kommission aus diesem ETS-System lagen allein im letzten Jahr bei mehr als 43 Milliarden Euro.

Statt ETS aufzuheben, weil es unsere eigenen Stahlwerke gefährdet und auch die übrige Industrie, führte die Kommission trickreich den CO2‑Zoll CBAM ein und weitete das ETS-System mal eben per Federstrich auf den Außenhandel aus – mit unkalkulierbaren Folgen für unsere Lieferketten.

Mehr als 1 Milliarde Euro fließen jetzt zusätzlich Jahr für Jahr in die Kasse der EU, während betroffene Unternehmen verzweifeln. Ein Schraubenimporteur muss jetzt etwa 6 Millionen Euro CBAM-Kosten pro Jahr zahlen – bei 90 Millionen Euro Umsatz. Diese Belastung wird an Maschinenbauer, Autohersteller und Verbraucher weitergegeben.

Erkennen Sie die unverschämte Umverteilung bei gleichzeitiger Gefährdung unserer Wirtschaft? Wir werden in ein kostspieliges, verlogenes Klimakorsett gezwungen. ETS verteuert die europäische Produktion, CBAM die Importe – und jetzt soll CBAM auf bis zu 457 weitere Produktgruppen ausgeweitet werden.

Der Effekt auf das Klima ist nicht messbar, aber unsere ökonomische Basis wird mit Sicherheit zerstört. Wir müssen ETS und CBAM jetzt stoppen. Deshalb braucht Europa die ESN, und Deutschland braucht die AfD.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, I have been looking forward to this new debating formula for weeks. I know we are short on time, so I am going to do it a bit staccato.

First, I wanted to say in the direction of gentlemen Canfin and Chahim that I very much agree with the importance they have underlined in terms of pushing this proposal forward from a climate perspective as well as from a competitiveness perspective. That is also the message I will convey to the Council. Then, they are also making a couple of suggestions about Article 27a. I know that that is a disputed area, if that is the way to to describe it. I look forward to continuing to engage on that and I am sure we can achieve our joint goal of dealing with exceptional circumstances while at the same time maintaining sufficient legal certainty.
Madam Gómez López asked me about own resources. There I just have to refer to the Commission proposal, I cannot deviate from that.

Madam Boylan was asking about technical assistance and using the money of CBAM exactly for that cause – that is exactly what we are doing. We are giving, I would say, a load of technical assistance to absolutely everyone who wants it and Europe continues to be the absolute front runner in terms of climate commitments and financing across the globe, full stop. So, we might not be doing it one‑on‑one, but we are doing more than our fair share.

To Madam Nerudová, I would want to say that I very much agree with keeping bureaucratic monsters out, but it was this Commission that actually took out 90 % of the companies from the scope. That is what we did. So, I think we have a bit of a track record, particularly in this domain.
To Mr Knotek, my only advice would be to further work on his analogies involving patients and hospitals.

Mr Vondra, that is a bit of a recap of the debate of last week. If you look at Europe and you look at who has the lowest energy prices, it is Finland. Why? Because they have a combination of renewables and a nuclear grid capacity, and that works phenomenally well. That is a recipe all should embark on. But let's not make the mistake to do as if just the ETS is the component that drives prices. That is driven, as Mr Vondra well knows, by the intrinsics first and foremost.
To Emma Wiesner, I would say that as much as I am a fan of recycling, this was maybe a bit too much frapper toujours compared to last week, but I very much enjoyed hearing it again.
I think I have done justice to everything that was more or less formulated as a question, I think. So, let me pause there because then that keeps one minute in the bank.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, dear Commissioner, I have a great deal of sympathy for the fact that those who emit CO₂ also want to know what the bill will look like. And we have a responsibility to ensure that changes we are making right now allow our businesses and voters to continue trusting us. Because when we say that, in this House, we bolster the 90 % fewer emissions by 2040, then we also need to deliver the tools to get there. One of them we are discussing today.

The Emissions Trading System already loses most people at the door, and it does not get any easier when we start to talk about the market stability reserve. But just like in any other market, the question is the same: what should it cost?

We, as politicians, should not set the price, but we must ensure that the rules and direction are transparent. We owe the business community one word: predictability. Otherwise, both the investments already made and those yet to be made will collapse like a house of cards.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señor comisario, después del verano más caluroso de nuestras vidas, cuando Naciones Unidas confirma que ya se ha aumentado un grado y medio la temperatura en la Tierra —hemos tenido hospitales colapsados en toda Europa y 200 millones de europeos sufriendo más de 35 grados a la vez, algo nunca visto— demostramos con este debate —y con la acción que hoy defendemos— que es posible no solo mantener y reforzar la acción climática, sino combatir el falso y estúpido dilema entre acción climática y competitividad; que es posible proteger nuestra industria y reforzar la acción climática.

¿Y cómo lo hacemos? Reforzando el ajuste de carbono en frontera, que protege a la industria para asegurar que, obviamente, en las importaciones en Europa se han aplicado los mismos estándares y regulación medioambiental; con el fondo de descarbonización temporal, para apoyar y acompañar a la industria que se está transformando, y manteniendo un mercado europeo de carbono fuerte y estable. Porque sabemos que no solo la acción climática protege nuestra industria y construye la competitividad del futuro, sino que, además, la estabilidad jurídica es lo que permite la inversión para el crecimiento presente y futuro.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, sono passati esattamente venti anni da quando è stata pensato, qui in Europa, il sistema di scambio di quote di emissione, quella odiosa tassa ambientale che coloro che producono, le tante industrie della nostra Europa, devono pagare per essere sostenibili.

A cosa ha portato questo? Alla recessione e alla deindustrializzazione della nostra Europa, con una concorrenza, a volte sleale, che arriva dal Sud-Est asiatico e che sta letteralmente scalzando tutta la nostra capacità produttiva. Non è solo il settore dell'automobile ma tutta l'industria pesante sta relegando la sua capacità produttiva.

A questo punto vi siete inventati il cosiddetto CBAM, il meccanismo per fare un vero e proprio dazio – perché so che è una parola che qua non si può utilizzare – ma un dazio per cercare di calmierare questo danno competitivo. Beh, però vi siete dimenticati gli agricoltori perché, togliendo l'articolo 27 e la clausola di salvaguardia, i fertilizzanti non verranno tutelati.
Questa Europa, così, non ci piace.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Meine sehr verehrten Damen und Herren! Immer wenn es um Gesetzgebung geht, hört man ja aus konservativen Kreisen fast schon religiös mantraartig: „Der Markt regelt das“. Und ich frage mich: Wieso gilt das eigentlich nicht beim CO2-Preis und beim Klimaschutz? Denn der funktioniert ja genauso. Wenn der CO2-Ausstoß sinkt, dann bleibt es günstig, und wenn nicht, dann zieht der Preis an. Und das ist auch gut so, denn erstens bekommen die E-Autos und die Wärmepumpen dann einen Wettbewerbsvorteil, und zweitens kann man mit den Einnahmen aus dem CO2-Preis Bürgerinnen und Bürger unterstützen.

Was jetzt hier beschlossen werden soll, dass ist eben kein Markt. Sobald der Preis anfängt zu wirken, soll er gedeckelt werden. Kein Markt, kein Klimaschutz, sondern Deckel. Wir haben einen Rauchmelder installiert und schrauben ihn jetzt ab, weil er möglicherweise anfängt zu piepen.

Nach diesem Hitzesommer, der uns in Europa 180 Milliarden EUR gekostet hat, sollte wirklich jeder auch in den hintersten Ecken dieses Parlaments wissen: Weniger Klimaschutz – das können wir uns wirklich nicht mehr leisten.

paragraphs.text: You claim that the conservatives are wrong we we say that CBAM or ETS are jamming and destroying our economy.
But please, explain to us: who else in the world – and in their right mind – is applying schemes that they claim are working in the EU?
Show me one country – not many countries – another country outside of the EU that applied something they are claiming is being applied in the EU which is making us all poorer.

paragraphs.text: I can tell you, for instance, that California, Canada and China, have emission trading systems.

But what I would like to understand from you is why are the prices in Romania, for instance, so high? Why are the electricity prices so high? And do you know what? It is precisely because there is a difference between Europe and China and the US. Europe is importing all of its energy – fossil energy that costs us a billion. And in addition, we have this cost from the climate crisis.

So if you want to do something against prices, then you have to switch to renewables because that brings prices down. And in Romania, we could see it when Bulgaria delivered energy from their batteries to Romania this summer when, because of the climate crisis, your nuclear power plants went down.

paragraphs.text: This is exactly the reason why the price of energy in Romania is higher, because a lot of insane politicians in Romania believe exactly what you are saying: that we should destroy our coal power plants, close down hydroelectric power plants and move on renewables.

The problem is this: what do you do if there's no sun, if there's no wind and if there's no water? This is the reason why the Romanians currently are paying pretty much the highest energy price in Europe. So the solution is to have energy addition, not energy transition. Keep the old energy sources and add new ones as much as you can.

Mladí ľudia nevidia v Európskej únii žiadnu budúcnosť. Energie, palivá, to všetko raketovo rastie. Výsledky vašej klimatickej politiky.

Ale namiesto toho, aby ste to zhodnotili a prijali opatrenia, ktoré povedú k tomu, že zastavíte tieto nezmyselné emisné povolenky, ktoré si musia spoločnosti kupovať, a naopak, netlačiť ich ešte aj do domácností, tak prichádzate s ďalšími a ďalšími nezmyslami. S emisnými normami, ktoré sa sprísňujú pre osobné aj nákladné automobily, s uhlíkovým clom, ktoré zase zaťaží naše domácnosti a ľudia v Európe budú platiť viac za svoj každodenný život.

Stále robíte všetko v rámci vašej zelenej klimatickej ideológie iba preto, aby ste zničili život ľuďom v Európskej únii. Výsledky však neprichádzajú žiadne. Vaše opatrenia nemajú nijaký vplyv na zmenu klímy. Nedokazujete nič z toho, čo ste ľuďom sľúbili. Akurát to robíte pre všetkých horšie. paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, stimați colegi, rapoartele pe care le avem acum de votat mâine pot să aducă un avantaj. În același timp, pot să fie aplicate prost, pentru că, domnule comisar, acest fond, temporar, pentru decarbonizare este foarte important, mecanismul pe care îl vom avea, tocmai pentru a nu distorsiona.

Dintotdeauna am susținut, dacă vreți, apărarea industriei și agriculturii din Uniunea Europeană, pentru că un producător, fie din industrie, fie un fermier, dacă din afară vin în interiorul pieței interne produse care nu respectă aceleași condiții de mediu, standarde sociale, și celelalte condiții, evident că sunt într-o competiție neloială.
De aceea cred că este foarte important dacă vrem să reindustrializăm, dacă vrem securitate alimentară, să avem aceleași condiții pentru produsele care intră din afara Uniunii Europene.
Și eu sper că reușim ca acest articol 27 a, cu amendamentele depuse mâine în plenară, să îmbunătățim, încât fermierii – am primit nenumărate scrisori – să poată să fie protejați.
Știm cum au crescut prețurile la îngrășăminte, știm ce probleme avem, cât e costul îngrășămintelor în costul producției fermierilor.
De aceea sper ca mâine să îmbunătățim aceste rapoarte.

Warming is caused by human activity. To have to explain that to assert this in an adult parliament is frankly depressing.

It is difficult to listen to conservatives criticising emissions trading when it was them that insisted on a market‑based intervention. It was them that insisted on 'cap and trade'. And I agree with MEP Chahim and with MEP Canfin that it is working and it is effective, and that CBAM is working and is effective.

I have criticised the simplification agenda when it has been deregulatory or when it has punished early adopters. However, it would be naive to ignore the realities and that is why our industry needs the competitiveness agenda. We need support in the face of the energy crisis, including through social climate plans, and it also needs support on carbon pricing.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, thank you very much. Not that many questions, but there are two things I do feel compelled to share here, given the nature of the debate.

Of course, you can debate what are the most effective measures. Of course, you can debate what type of mix you need to have in terms of renewables and nuclear and so on. Of course, you can debate what works best in terms of the level playing field. But if you deny the economic cost of climate change, you're deep into the domain of voodoo economics, and I would suggest we steer away from that.

Secondly, why are energy prices in Europe so high? Because we import more than 80 % of the gas, more than 95 % of the oil – and the price tag only since Hormuz has gone up by an additional half a billion every single day. That is money European citizens and European companies are paying.

The only way out of this nightmare is more dirt cheap, Europe-made energy, and that means renewables, it means nuclear, it means green investments, it means interconnectors, it means geothermal – that whole mix with more speed.
Finally, I am still pondering whether we have further enriched this style of debate, but that is, of course, not up to me; that is up to Parliament.

Maybe use some googling and find out. The world is following the EU. And why? Because they see that with the revenues you can decarbonise your industry. We have doubled the Modernisation Fund to show solidarity within Europe. That's what you conclude if you take the facts and read the legislation and read what we work on.

It's ridiculous only making noise with zero effect and zero contributions to the legislation. A fool can ask more questions than ten wise people can answer. And I can tell you the difference between stupidity and intelligence is that intelligence is limited.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, je me réjouis de la qualité du débat, à l'exception des interventions permanentes des députés d'extrême droite qui, pendant une heure, ont exprimé des points de vue climatosceptiques niant l'évidence même.

Non, Monsieur, le rythme actuel de réchauffement climatique n'a rien à voir avec celui du passé. Toutes les études scientifiques le démontrent. Non, Monsieur, ce n'est pas parce qu'on décarbone, qu'on investit dans les renouvelables et l'énergie nucléaire, que les prix de l'énergie sont très élevés. C'est exactement le contraire.

C'est parce qu'en Roumanie, c'est parce qu'en Italie vous êtes totalement dépendants du gaz que, précisément, vous avez une énergie qui est bien plus chère qu'en France, qu'en Espagne, qu'en Suède. C'est votre responsabilité. C'est parce que vous n'avez pas investi dans les technologies vertes que nous, nous voulons voir développer – que nous avons commencé à développer – que vous rendez les gens dépendants d'une énergie très chère, très polluante et totalement importée.

Alors, je sais que cela ne vous pose aucun problème d'être dépendant de Vladimir Poutine. Je sais que ça ne vous pose aucun problème d'être dépendant des États-Unis, de Donald Trump. Mais nous, nous réellement patriotes européens, nous souverainistes européens – les vrais – qui voulons créer l'Europe-puissance, oui, ça nous gêne d'être dépendants des puissances fossiles.

C'est pour ça qu'on a besoin du marché du carbone. C'est pour ça qu'on a besoin d'un prix du carbone, du MACF. Mais c'est pour ça qu'on continuera à se battre contre tous vos mensonges, contre toutes vos inepties. Vous pouvez compter sur nous.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, ho ascoltato con grande attenzione tutti gli interventi e ringrazio i colleghi per i loro contributi. È del tutto naturale che, su un tema così rilevante come quello dell'ETS, vi siano sensibilità e posizioni diverse in quest'Aula.

Stiamo affrontando alcuni tra i dossier più complessi e politicamente sensibili di questa legislatura, in un momento in cui la concorrenza internazionale è durissima e non sempre leale, e dopo un'estate che ci ha fatto sentire con mano cos'è il cambiamento climatico.

Tuttavia, voglio respingere con chiarezza quella che ritengo essere una falsa dicotomia: l'idea che ci si debba schierare da una parte con l'ambizione climatica o dall'altra con l'industria europea. Scegliere di migliorare l'ETS o il CBAM non può significare abbandonare l'industria e i nostri lavoratori e, allo stesso tempo, scegliere di difendere la competitività delle nostre imprese non può significare rinunciare ai nostri obiettivi climatici.

L'Europa non può e non deve scegliere tra queste due sfide: al contrario, dobbiamo avere l'ambizione e la capacità di tenerle insieme. È una necessità strategica, perché un'industria innovativa e decarbonizzata è l'unica che potrà essere davvero competitiva a livello globale nei prossimi anni.

Così come una transizione ecologica non può funzionare se contribuirà a deindustrializzare il nostro continente o a far delocalizzare le nostre imprese. I provvedimenti che stiamo discutendo, però, stanno dimostrando che, con fatica, ascoltandoci e venendoci incontro, siamo in grado di trovare dei compromessi che trovano il giusto equilibrio tra queste due sfide.

È esattamente questo il senso del lavoro che io e gli altri relatori abbiamo portato avanti in queste settimane nelle nostre commissioni. Io credo che, col voto di domani, potremo dimostrare che, in mesi in cui sarà molto difficile trovare accordi su questi provvedimenti, e penso a tutta la prosecuzione dell'ETS, beh, però abbiamo un metodo di lavoro che ci consente di farlo, trovando il punto migliore di accordo tra la maggior parte di noi.

paragraphs.text: Anna Zalewska (ECR), na piśmiePani Przewodnicząca, Panie Komisarzu, chcę zwrócić uwagę na problem, którego nie rozwiąże samo tworzenie kolejnych funduszy pomocowych.W moich regionach, na Dolnym Śląsku i Opolszczyźnie, przemysł daje pracę łącznie około 362 tysiącom osób. Za tą liczbą stoją przedsiębiorstwa, rodziny i całe lokalne gospodarki.Dla wielu firm problemem nie jest tylko wysokość kosztów, ale również zachowanie płynności finansowej. Przedsiębiorstwo może stracić kontrakty, zdolność do inwestowania i płynność, a nawet zbankrutować, zanim otrzyma przewidziane wsparcie.Firmy nie chcą jednak żyć z kolejnych rekompensat. Chcą stać na własnych nogach, inwestować, rozwijać się i konkurować na równych zasadach.Europa Środkowo Wschodnia przeszła już głęboką transformację gospodarczą. Nie możemy dopuścić do utraty kolejnych zakładów i miejsc pracy.Dotyczy to także sektora stalowego. Europejscy producenci ponoszą wysokie koszty związane z ETS. CBAM powinien sprawić, by importowane towary ponosiły porównywalny koszt emisji do tego, który ponoszą producenci w Unii Europejskiej.Musimy uważać, aby rezultatem naszej polityki nie było zamykanie produkcji w Europie i zastępowanie jej importem z państw trzecich. Nie możemy dopuścić do sytuacji, w której Europa będzie korzystać z tych samych produktów, ale zamiast produkować je u siebie, będzie je sprowadzać z zagranicy. Wtedy stracimy miejsca pracy i europejskie moce produkcyjne, nie rozwiązując problemu emisji w skali globalnej.

interventions.speaker_label: Stéphane Séjourné, Vice-président exécutif de la Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Mesdames et Messieurs les députés, les marchés publics représentent chaque année en Europe plus de 2 000 milliards d'euros, soit près de 15 % du PIB européen. Nous avons donc entre les mains un levier économique considérable, une manne pouvant être mieux mobilisée pour la cohésion sociale, pour la décarbonation, pour l'innovation, pour la sécurité économique de l'Europe. C'est pourquoi cette réforme de la commande publique poursuit aujourd'hui deux objectifs: d'abord une simplification massive, puis une utilisation plus stratégique de cet argent public.

D'abord, peut-être commencer par la simplification, puisque les règles qui encadrent la commande publique en Europe représentent aujourd'hui près de 900 pages de textes européens, auxquels s'ajoutent toutes les surtranspositions et les transpositions nationales. Un règlement, une directive, trois directives, plus d'une vingtaine de règlements. Nous mettons fin à cette complexité en proposant un règlement unique, trois procédures au lieu de cinq, une plateforme numérique accessible dans toutes les langues de l'Union européenne et, ensuite, une commande publique qui nous permettra d'utiliser les critères plus facilement et de gagner en lisibilité pour les acheteurs publics.

Ensuite, une commande plus stratégique: sur ces 2 000 milliards d'euros, 600 milliards d'euros sont couverts par la législation que nous vous proposons. C'est l'équivalent du plan de relance Next generation EU, c'est l'équivalent de trois budgets européens par an si nous regardons ces sommes et, effectivement, chaque année, c'est presque autant que le déficit d'investissement que cible Mario Draghi dans son rapport. Tout ça pour vous dire que l'argent public doit servir nos objectifs. Une modification d'un certain nombre de critères, et une réorientation plus stratégique de cette dépense publique qui a lieu tous les ans, sont dorénavant importantes dans le cadre de nos priorités.

Alors, le nouveau standard, c'est le meilleur rapport qualité-prix et non plus le seul prix. C'est le principe de ce texte. Nos choix doivent pouvoir répondre aux exigences sociales, environnementales, aux enjeux d'innovation et de souveraineté que nous défendons. Je le dis clairement devant vous, ce texte donne aussi aux acheteurs publics les outils d'une véritable préférence européenne, dans le respect de nos engagements internationaux et du principe de réciprocité.

Ce texte est également un outil pensé pour donner des leviers à ceux qui achètent, à ceux qui investissent pour notre avenir, et donne énormément de possibilités à tous ceux qui, aujourd'hui, font de la commande publique uniquement un acte administratif. Transformer cet acte administratif également pour nous en stratégie d'achats publics européens.

Alors, Mesdames, Messieurs les députés, ce débat est l'occasion d'échanger sur ces ambitions. La Commission européenne se réjouit de pouvoir commencer la discussion entre les colégislateurs sur ce règlement européen.

paragraphs.text: Sehr geehrte Frau Präsidentin, Herr Exekutivvizepräsident, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Angesichts globaler Krisen und innerer Herausforderungen sehen wir jeden Tag deutlicher, wir müssen in Europa auf allen Ebenen handlungsfähiger und schneller werden. Überall braucht es eine öffentliche Hand, die ihre Aufgaben zuverlässig erfüllt, die wichtige Zukunftsinvestitionen zügig umsetzt und die schnell auf neue Entwicklungen reagieren kann. Das Vergaberecht ist dafür das zentrale Werkzeug.

Mit der Reform des Vergaberechts entscheiden wir über die Handlungsfähigkeit der gesamten Europäischen Union – von der internationalen Bühne bis zur kleinsten Kommune. Handlungsfähigkeit bedeutet, bürokratische Lasten für wirklich jeden abzubauen.

Die Zusammenlegung mehrerer Rechtsakte und die im Vorschlag bereits enthaltenen Vereinfachungen begrüßen wir. Wir müssen dafür sorgen, dass diese bei den Anwendern in jeder Gemeinde ankommen. Die Möglichkeit, künftig stärker auf Qualitätskriterien statt einzig auf den Preis setzen zu können, ist für uns ein guter Fortschritt. Allerdings ist auch klar, die Auftraggeber vor Ort wissen am besten, wann und welche Kriterien sinnvoll berücksichtigt werden können. Sie brauchen einen rechtssicheren Rahmen und Flexibilität statt neuer bürokratischer Pflichten aus Brüssel.

Handlungsfähigkeit bedeutet für uns schnelle und einfache digitale Vergabe. Eine digitale Plattform, die bestehende Systeme integriert, hat großes Potenzial, die Verfahren tatsächlich zu beschleunigen und zu vereinfachen. Entscheidend ist, dass diese auch zuverlässig funktioniert.
Liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen, entscheidend wird für uns sein, dass das Vergabeverfahren auf ein handlungsfähiges Europa setzt.

Sehr geehrte Frau Präsidentin, Herr Exekutivvizepräsident, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Angesichts globaler Krisen und innerer Herausforderungen sehen wir jeden Tag deutlicher, wir müssen in Europa auf allen Ebenen handlungsfähiger und schneller werden. Überall braucht es eine öffentliche Hand, die ihre Aufgaben zuverlässig erfüllt, die wichtige Zukunftsinvestitionen zügig umsetzt und die schnell auf neue Entwicklungen reagieren kann. Das Vergaberecht ist dafür das zentrale Werkzeug.

Mit der Reform des Vergaberechts entscheiden wir über die Handlungsfähigkeit der gesamten Europäischen Union – von der internationalen Bühne bis zur kleinsten Kommune. Handlungsfähigkeit bedeutet, bürokratische Lasten für wirklich jeden abzubauen.

Die Zusammenlegung mehrerer Rechtsakte und die im Vorschlag bereits enthaltenen Vereinfachungen begrüßen wir. Wir müssen dafür sorgen, dass diese bei den Anwendern in jeder Gemeinde ankommen. Die Möglichkeit, künftig stärker auf Qualitätskriterien statt einzig auf den Preis setzen zu können, ist für uns ein guter Fortschritt. Allerdings ist auch klar, die Auftraggeber vor Ort wissen am besten, wann und welche Kriterien sinnvoll berücksichtigt werden können. Sie brauchen einen rechtssicheren Rahmen und Flexibilität statt neuer bürokratischer Pflichten aus Brüssel.

Handlungsfähigkeit bedeutet für uns schnelle und einfache digitale Vergabe. Eine digitale Plattform, die bestehende Systeme integriert, hat großes Potenzial, die Verfahren tatsächlich zu beschleunigen und zu vereinfachen. Entscheidend ist, dass diese auch zuverlässig funktioniert.

Liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen, entscheidend wird für uns sein, dass das Vergabeverfahren auf ein handlungsfähiges Europa setzt.
